recommendation: Keep this commit as-is. It is a bounded current-build repair to the applied FHIR-16188 guidance; further work is only needed if FHIR-I reopens the modifier policy itself.
issue_request: FHIR-16188 was Published with resolution Not Persuasive with Modification. The issue asked to remove or replace Is-Modifier because the prior definition seemed broad enough to make every element a modifier and hard to apply consistently; FHIR-I instead decided to keep Is-Modifier and add clearer Conformance-page guidance defining testable boundaries.
initial_application: The issue was applied by git-svn commit 005b06c3a41f6322d2baf380d1b627a57d174639 / svn r14216, which added the current litmus-test definition to source/conformance-rules.html and introduced a modifier-extension cross-reference in source/extensibility.html. The substantive rule remains present in current source.
additional_context: source/hierarchy.xml includes both conformance-rules.html and extensibility.html in the current Foundation documentation, so both are in build scope. Later modifier-related source history, including FHIR-40769, reinforces conformance-rules.html as the central definition. Zulip evidence from the July 2018 Observation discussion matches the applied false-interpretation criterion, and direct Zulip/Confluence searches found no conflicting FHIR-16188 record.
reconciliation: Changed source/extensibility.html so the modifier-extension guidance links to conformance-rules.html#isModifier instead of the non-existent conformance-rules.html#modifier anchor. No redundant prose was added because the FHIR-16188 clarification is already present in source/conformance-rules.html.
source_changes: source/extensibility.html:328 changed the modifier rules cross-reference from conformance-rules.html#modifier to conformance-rules.html#isModifier.

related_jiras.note: Observation.focus modifier debate was cited from FHIR-16188 discussion and helped clarify the false-interpretation test, but it is a separate Observation decision.
Later ElementDefinition.isModifier source changes point readers to the conformance-rules section, reinforcing that the FHIR-16188 rule remains the central definition.

evidence_items.summary: Current Conformance rules define a modifier as an element that cannot be safely ignored because it may make the containing element or descendants diverge from their definitions.
